questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: Which of the following is contraindicated in a neonate with scaphoid abdomen?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Bag & Mask ventilation

Scaphoid abdomen in a neonate → think Congenital Diaphragmatic Hernia (CDH)

What happens with bag & mask ventilation:

Air goes into stomach + intestines→ while these organs are already in the thorax → They inflate further → compress lungs more →  Leads to severe respiratory compromise.

Intubation

Directly ventilates lungs ; Avoids air going into stomach. Hence preferred.

Positive pressure ventilation (after intubation)

Safe when airway is secured→ ie useful after intubation.

In this case → Immediate intubation with nasogastric tube to decompress stomach

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: Which of the following is incorrect about tension pneumothorax?
options: Improper dressing of an open chest wound can lead to tension pneumothorax
Simple pneumothorax can never become tension pneumothorax
It may occur after mechanical ventilation with PEEP
Severe chest trauma with rib fractures and spine injuries can lead to it
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Simple pneumothorax can never become tension pneumothorax

A simple pneumothorax can progress to a tension pneumothorax→ when a one-way valve mechanism develops → air enters the pleural space but cannot escape.

✔️ Improper dressing of an open chest wound → tension pneumothorax

If all sides are sealed tightly→ air gets trapped → acts like a one-way valve

✔️ Mechanical ventilation with PEEP

Positive pressure pushes more air into pleural space → increases risk of tension pneumothorax.

✔️ Severe chest trauma with rib fractures and spine injuries can be associated

Lung laceration + air leak → can evolve into tension pneumothorax

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: Which of the following is the correct order of steps for trauma management as per ATLS guidelines? 1. Circulation with hemorrhage control 2. Airway with cervical spine stabilization 3. Disability assessment 4. Control of catastrophic bleeding
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. 4, 2, 1, 3

The initial assessment of trauma follows the ATLS primary survey. In modern trauma care, catastrophic external hemorrhage is controlled before the standard ABCDE sequence, as uncontrolled bleeding is an immediately reversible cause of death. This modified approach is remembered as ABCDE.

The correct sequence is:

1. Control of catastrophic bleeding
2. Airway with cervical spine stabilization (A)
3. Breathing (B) (not listed in the options)
4. Circulation with hemorrhage control (C)
5. Disability assessment (D)
6. Exposure and environmental control (E) (not listed in the options)

Among the given options, this corresponds to: 4 → 2 → 1 → 3

Why not the other options?

• They do not follow the ATLS primary survey sequence and incorrectly prioritize circulation or disability before airway after controlling catastrophic hemorrhage.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: Which of the following is the likely diagnosis in a patient with thyroid growth with multiple lytic lesions in the skull?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Follicular thyroid cancer

✔️ Option B: Follicular thyroid carcinoma characteristically spreads by hematogenous route rather than lymphatics, commonly metastasizes to bone, producing multiple lytic skull lesions.

❌Option A:Papillary carcinoma : spreads via lymphatics, presents with cervical nodal metastasis.

❌Option C: Hurthle cell carcinoma is aggressive but not associated with lytic bone metastases.

❌Option D: Lymphoma presents as Rapidly enlarging thyroid mass, not linked to skull lytic lesions

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: Which of the following provides the most accurate information for reporting the 'T stage' of esophageal carcinoma? (NEET PG 2015)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Endoscopic USG

Endoscopic ultrasonography (EUS) is the most accurate modality for determining the T stage (depth of tumor invasion) in esophageal carcinoma. EUS provides highly detailed images of the layers of the esophageal wall, allowing precise determination of tumor depth invasion through visualization of the mucosa, submucosa, muscularis propria, and adventitia.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: Which of the following statements are correct regarding ABCDE of trauma care? I. A stands for Airway with cervical spine protection. II. B stands for Breathing and ventilation. III. C stands for Control of massive external haemorrhage. IV. D stands for Disability (Neurological status). Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. I, II and IV

The ABCDE approach is the cornerstone of the Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS) protocol and is designed to identify and treat life-threatening injuries in order of priority. Each step must be completed and stabilized before moving to the next. The following statements are correct:

• I. A stands for Airway with cervical spine protection: The airway should be assessed and secured while maintaining cervical spine immobilization until spinal injury is excluded.
• II. B stands for Breathing and ventilation: Assess chest movement, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, breath sounds, and treat life-threatening thoracic injuries (e.g., tension pneumothorax).
• IV. D stands for Disability (Neurological status): Rapid neurological assessment includes:

• Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS)
• Pupillary size and reaction
• Limb movement
• Blood glucose (to exclude hypoglycemia)

Why is III incorrect?

• III. C stands for Control of massive external haemorrhage: In ATLS, C stands for Circulation with hemorrhage control, not merely control of massive external hemorrhage. It includes:

• Assessment of pulse and blood pressure
• Control of all bleeding
• IV access and fluid/blood resuscitation
• Assessment of tissue perfusion ⭐

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: Which of the following statements are correct regarding primary survey/management of traumatic head injury patient? I. Ensure adequate oxygenation and circulation II. Exclude hypoglycaemia III. Check for mechanism of injury IV. Check pupil size and response Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. I, II and IV

The primary survey of a patient with traumatic head injury follows the Advanced Trauma Life Support (ATLS) principles, with emphasis on identifying and correcting life-threatening conditions before proceeding to a detailed neurological assessment.

The priorities are:

• Airway maintenance with cervical spine protection
• Breathing and adequate oxygenation
• Circulation and hemorrhage control
• Disability (neurological assessment)
• Exposure

The following are essential components of the primary survey:

• I. Ensure adequate oxygenation and circulation: Hypoxia and hypotension are the two most important preventable causes of secondary brain injury and should be corrected immediately.
• II. Exclude hypoglycaemia: Hypoglycemia can mimic altered sensorium and should always be ruled out in any unconscious or confused patient.
• IV. Check pupil size and response: Pupillary examination is part of the Disability (D) assessment and helps detect raised intracranial pressure or transtentorial herniation.

Why is III incorrect?

• III. Check for mechanism of injury: Although the mechanism of injury is important during the secondary survey and history-taking, it is not a priority in the primary survey, which focuses on immediate life-saving interventions.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: Which of the following statements are correct regarding renal cell carcinoma? 1. It arises from the epithelium of the proximal convoluted tubule. 2. It has a female preponderance. 3. Major subtypes are clear cell, papillary and chromophobe. 4. Surgery is the mainstay of treatment for organ-confined disease. Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1, 3 and 4

Why is C correct?

• 1. It arises from the epithelium of the proximal convoluted tubule. ✅

• Most RCCs, particularly clear cell RCC, originate from the proximal tubular epithelial cells.

• 2. It has a female preponderance. ❌

• RCC is more common in males, with a male-to-female ratio of approximately 2:1.

• 3. Major subtypes are clear cell\, papillary and chromophobe. ✅

• These are the three major histological subtypes:

• Clear cell RCC (70–80%)
• Papillary RCC (10–15%)
• Chromophobe RCC (5%)

• 4. Surgery is the mainstay of treatment for organ-confined disease. ✅

• Partial nephrectomy (preferred for T1 tumors) or radical nephrectomy is the standard treatment for localized RCC.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: Which of the following statements are correct regarding the fluid management of pediatric inpatients with burn injuries? 1. The Parkland formula estimates the amount of fluid to be replaced over 24 hours. 2. Volume of fluid (mL) = 4 mL × Weight (kg) × Total body surface area burn (%). 3. Additional maintenance fluid therapy is also to be given to the child. 4. Half of the resuscitation volume should be given over 6 hours and the remaining half over the next 18 hours. Select the answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. 1, 2 and 3

Fluid resuscitation is the cornerstone of management in major pediatric burn injuries. The Parkland formula is used to estimate the initial 24-hour fluid requirement, but unlike adults, children also require additional maintenance fluids because of their higher metabolic rate and limited glycogen stores.

Why is B correct?

• 1. The Parkland formula estimates the amount of fluid to be replaced over 24 hours. ✅

• It calculates the initial fluid requirement for the first 24 hours after a burn.

• 2. Volume of fluid (mL) = 4 mL × Weight (kg) × Total body surface area burn (%). ✅

• This is the Parkland formula using Ringer’s lactate.

• 3. Additional maintenance fluid therapy is also to be given to the child. ✅

• Children require maintenance fluids in addition to Parkland resuscitation to meet their physiological needs and prevent hypoglycemia.

• 4. Half of the resuscitation volume should be given over 6 hours and the remaining half over the next 18 hours. ❌

• The correct regimen is:

• First half over the first 8 hours from the time of burn
• Remaining half over the next 16 hours

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: Which of the following statements is false about the given condition?
options: Repeated radical surgery every 24 hours may be required
This is a case of Meleney's gangrene
Caused by beta-hemolytic streptococcus, may be polymicrobial
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. Hyperbaric oxygen has no role

The correct answer is: D) Hyperbaric oxygen has no role — this statement is false.

The image and options describe necrotizing fasciitis (Meleney’s gangrene).

Key Features of Necrotizing Fasciitis

• Severe pain out of proportion
• Skin discoloration
• Necrosis / gangrene
• Rapid progression

Usually polymicrobial infection(Group A β-hemolytic Streptococcus, Staphylococcus, Anaerobes, gram-negative bacteria)

So option C is true.

Management :

1. Emergency surgical debridement

Repeated radical debridement every 24 hours may be required

So Option A is correct.

2. Broad-spectrum antibiotics (like carbapenems, piperacillin-tazobactam)

3. Hyperbaric oxygen therapy

Improves tissue oxygenation; Helps control anaerobic infection

Therefore saying “Hyperbaric oxygen has no role” is false.

Feature | Necrotizing Fasciitis

| ------- | ---------------------

| Also called | Meleney’s gangrene

| Infection type | Polymicrobial

| Treatment | Urgent surgical debridement

| Adjunct therapy | Hyperbaric oxygen

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: Which of the following structures is affected in the disease shown in the image below?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Great saphenous vein

The great saphenous vein (GSV):

• Runs along the medial aspect of the leg and thigh
• Drains into the femoral vein at the saphenofemoral junction

When its valves become incompetent, blood flows backward (venous reflux) leading to:

• Dilated tortuous superficial veins
• Chronic venous hypertension
• Varicose veins

Typical Features of Great Saphenous Vein Varicosities

• Medial leg involvement
• Bulging tortuous veins

❌ B) Deep veins

Deep veins are not visible externally, so they do not produce visible varicosities like in the image.

❌ C) Perforator veins

Perforators connect superficial veins to deep veins.

Their incompetence can contribute to disease but does not create the long medial varicose pattern seen here.

❌ D) Short saphenous vein

The short saphenous vein runs along the posterior aspect of the leg and drains into the popliteal vein.

Varicosities would therefore appear behind the calf, not along the medial leg.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: Which of the following types of renal stones are produced by laxative abuse?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: B. Ammonium urate

Ammonium urate stones are classically associated with chronic laxative abuse, chronic diarrhea, inflammatory bowel disease, and conditions causing prolonged gastrointestinal bicarbonate and fluid loss. These stones form due to volume depletion, acidic urine, and increased urinary ammonium excretion.

Chronic laxative abuse leads to:

• Persistent diarrhea
• Dehydration and hypovolemia
• Metabolic acidosis
• Increased renal ammonium production and excretion

These factors promote the formation of ammonium urate calculi.

Characteristic Associations of Common Renal Stones

| Stone Type | Characteristic Association

| ---------- | --------------------------

| Calcium oxalate | Hypercalciuria, hyperparathyroidism, ethylene glycol poisoning

| Struvite (Magnesium ammonium phosphate) | Urease-positive infections (Proteus, Klebsiella)

| Uric acid | Gout, tumor lysis syndrome, myeloproliferative disorders

| Ammonium urate | Laxative abuse, chronic diarrhea, malnutrition

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: Which of these is not a component/adjunct of the primary survey in trauma?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: D. CECT

Primary survey means quick bedside assessment for unstable patients.

Includes : chest X-ray, pelvic X-ray, eFAST, ECG, ABG, NG tube, and catheter.

In contrast: CECT needs a stable patient , is time-consuming

Hence, CECT is part of secondary survey and only for stable patients, not during initial resuscitation.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: Which of these is true about intermittent claudication?
options: Pain occurs on walking a fixed distance and is relieved by rest
Pain occurs immediately on standing and improves on bending forward
Pain is worse at night in bed and at rest
Pain occurs on taking the first step
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Pain occurs on walking a fixed distance and is relieved by rest

Option A .✅ Pain occurs on walking a fixed distance and is relieved by rest

→ Intermittent claudication (PAD) is exertional leg pain

• Occurs after walking a predictable distance, relieved by rest.
• Because:  Exercise ↑ oxygen demand → stenosed arteries can’t supply → ischemic pain; rest ↓ demand → pain relieved.

Option B ❌ Pain occurs immediately on standing and improves on bending forward

→ Neurogenic claudication (lumbar canal stenosis)

Because : Standing (extension) narrows spinal canal → nerve compression; bending forward (flexion) widens canal → relief

Option C ❌ Pain is worse at night in bed and at rest

→ Critical limb ischemia: Because:

• Severe arterial compromise causes→ inadequate blood flow even at rest
• Becomes worse on elevation (↓ perfusion) and relieved in dependent position.

Option D ❌ Pain occurs on taking the first step

→ Plantar fasciitis Because :

• Tight plantar fascia after rest →there is sudden stretch on first step → causes pain.
• Improves with continued walking.

Boyd’s classification of intermittent claudication

• Class 1: Pain on walking, Reduces with continued walking
• Class 2: Pain on walking, Patient continues to walk despite pain
• Class 3: Pain forces patient to stop

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: Which of these is/are included as a part of primary survey in trauma? 1. Endotracheal intubation 2. Chest X-ray 3. Plain CT 4. ICD insertion
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. 1, 2 and 4 are correct

Primary survey in trauma follows the ABCDE approach (ATLS guidelines)

• A – Airway (with cervical spine protection)
• B – Breathing
• C – Circulation
• D – Disability
• E – Exposure

-In the primary survey of a trauma patient, life-saving interventions like ET intubation, bedside chest X-ray, and ICD insertion are performed to stabilize the patient.

1. Endotracheal intubation

• Done in Airway (A): in cases of Airway compromise / GCS ≤ 8 / Severe facial trauma.

2. Chest X-ray

• Done as a bedside adjunct to primary survey.
• Helps detect emergencies like Pneumothorax, Hemothorax → guides immediate management

3. Plain CT -Part of secondary survey

• Requires patient transfer + time and cannot be done in unstable patients.
• Hence, comes under secondary survey

4. ICD insertion (Intercostal Drain)

• Done in Breathing (B): for indications like Tension pneumothorax, Massive hemothorax

→ guides in immediate life-saving intervention

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: Which one of the following statements regarding inherited cancer syndromes is not correct?
options: Pituitary tumours are seen in MEN type 1.
Brain tumours are seen in Li-Fraumeni syndrome.
Breast cancer is seen in FAP syndrome.
Prostate cancer is seen in familial breast cancer syndrome.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Breast cancer is seen in FAP syndrome.

1. Pituitary tumours in MEN 1: Correct.

• MEN 1 is characterized by tumors of the “3 Ps”:

• Parathyroid
• Pituitary
• Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors

2. Brain tumours in Li-Fraumeni syndrome: Correct.

• Li-Fraumeni syndrome is due to TP53 mutation and predisposes to multiple malignancies, including brain tumors, sarcomas, breast cancer and adrenocortical carcinoma.

3. Breast cancer in FAP: Incorrect.

• Familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP) is caused by an APC mutation and primarily predisposes to colorectal adenocarcinoma and other GI/duodenal malignancies.
• Breast cancer is not a characteristic malignancy of FAP.

4. Prostate cancer in familial breast cancer syndrome: Correct.

• BRCA1/BRCA2-associated hereditary breast/ovarian cancer syndrome, particularly BRCA2, is also associated with an increased risk of prostate cancer.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: Which patient category is classified as "green" according to the triage system?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A. Ambulatory patients

“Green tag” = walking wounded, minor injuries, ambulatory, can safely wait for treatment. Yellow = urgent; red = immediate; black = deceased/unsalvageable.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: Which type of thyroid carcinoma has the least likelihood of lymph node metastasis? (NEET PG 2017)
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Follicular carcinoma of the thyroid

Follicular carcinoma of the thyroid has the least likelihood of lymph node metastasis among the given options. Follicular carcinoma typically presents as a solitary thyroid nodule with a strong tendency for hematogenous spread rather than lymphatic spread. While it commonly metastasizes to bones (particularly thoracic vertebrae and skull) via blood vessels, lymph node involvement is rare, except in the Hurthle cell variant which may show lymph node metastases.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: While performing triage in response to a disaster emergency, commonly an internationally accepted four-colour code system is used. Which one among the following four-colour categories represents the highest priority for emergency response?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Red

Triage is the process of sorting patients according to the severity of injury and urgency of treatment during disasters or mass casualty incidents, so that limited resources are used to save the maximum number of lives.

The international four-colour triage system is:

• Red – Immediate: Life-threatening injuries requiring immediate treatment (highest priority).
• Yellow – Delayed: Serious injuries requiring treatment, but can safely wait.
• Green – Minor: Walking wounded; treatment can be delayed.
• Black – Dead/Expectant: Dead or injuries incompatible with survival despite available resources.

questions.subject: Surgery
questions.text: LIFT procedure in fistula surgery stands for:
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: C. Ligation of intersphincteric fistula tract

LIFT (Ligation of Intersphincteric Fistula Tract) is a sphincter-preserving procedure used for the treatment of fistula-in-ano.

Principle

• The fistulous tract is identified in the intersphincteric plane.
• The tract is ligated close to the internal opening.
• The tract is divided, thereby disconnecting the internal opening from the external tract.
• This eradicates the fistula while preserving the anal sphincters.

Advantages

• Preserves continence (minimal risk of fecal incontinence).
• Suitable for complex transsphincteric fistulas.
• Less sphincter damage compared with fistulotomy.
• Good healing rates with low morbidity.

High-Yield MCQ Points

• LIFT = Ligation of Intersphincteric Fistula Tract.
• Indicated mainly for transsphincteric fistula-in-ano.
• A sphincter-saving procedure.
• Preferred when preservation of continence is important.
